terminologyReview: Guideline clarification: the revised distinction in references/common.md and references/ga.md is correct. The evidence agrees on three points. intl-workerd.json shows Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat unsupported (English output) for eo, be and ga, while Intl.PluralRules returns native categories for all 18 locales. InstructionTemplates (packages/shared/src/instruction-template.ts) builds Intl.PluralRules for the content language and throws when a catalog omits a native count variant or a message. BotText.andList and transcriptLabelList join items only through the catalog's formatting.* patterns. So Bickr's own formatters never 'silently return English'; the English fallback is only a property of the platform Intl list and relative-time formatters, which Bickr does not use for these strings. One leftover: references/eo.md line 7 still says 'The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work.' It should use the same wording as common.md and ga.md (be.md already does). This is a guideline edit only and changes no frozen English unit.

For Esperanto specifically, references/eo.md line 7 still carries the old sentence "The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work." It should say what common.md says: Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English in Workers, Intl.PluralRules supports eo, and Bickr uses explicit catalog patterns. The final eo catalog has all explicit list (formatting.*) and relative-time (time.*) patterns, so Bickr output is unaffected.

Esperanto terminology follows the lead decisions. "en via rolo" is used in every addressee-role instruction (no rolante left). "resumo de memoroj" is used in every compaction unit, with one remaining exception in tools.provide_summary (new finding). JSON-objekto is used in 26 units, and only the four malformed-call units keep "objekto JSON" (optional alignment proposed). Lists omit the serial comma. "Poste voku" is used for "call next", "referenco" for ref in prose, and "ĵetono" for token.

Quoted-string phrase: "enfermitaj en citiloj" is correct and clear. Ordinary Esperanto derivation also allows the noun-derived verb "citili" (participle "citilitaj"); unfamiliarity is a readability reason, not a grammar defect. "cititaj" would mean "cited" and is the less precise choice.

terminologyReview: Guideline corrections: all are accurate and stated as native instructions rather than copied English modals. (1) eo.md and be.md now say what common.md and ga.md say: in Workers, Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for these languages, Intl.PluralRules supports them, and Bickr uses explicit catalog patterns and rejects missing entries. This matches intl-workerd.json and InstructionTemplates, which throws on a missing message or count variant. The old "runtime formatters silently return English" wording is gone. (2) fr.md, pt.md and it.md now say that count parameters render ASCII digits, that a category does not insert million/milliard, milhão/milhões or milione/milioni, that de/di follows only the written numeral construction, and that many may match other for an all-digit numeral. This matches String(value) in instruction-template.ts and the platform labels "il y a 1 000 000 minutes", "há 1.000.000 minutos" and "1.000.000 minuti fa". (3) de.md separates positive obligations (Sie müssen) from prohibitions (dürfen nicht), states that "Darf nicht leer sein" is the form for a required nonempty value, and warns that "muss nicht" means need not. That is the correct German modal system: English "must not" maps to "darf nicht", not to "muss nicht".

Esperanto: JSON-objekto and resumo de memoroj are now uniform across the catalog. The explicit "enfermitaj en citiloj" phrase is retained by lead decision; the noun-derived verb citili is grammatical but less familiar.

grok.terminologyReview: The revised references are accurate and do not copy English modal labels onto native grammar. common.md, ga.md, eo.md, and be.md name Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat as the Workers fallback for Esperanto, Belarusian, and Irish. Intl.PluralRules supports their categories. Bickr catalog formatters reject a missing entry and use explicit native patterns, so they do not silently return English. French, Portuguese, and Italian count parameters insert digits. A many category does not insert million, milliard, milhão, milhões, milione, or milioni. de or di appears only when the written numeral construction needs it. Native Intl.RelativeTimeFormat gives a round million a direct numeric plural label. German positive obligations use müssen. A negative command uses nicht with the imperative, and a prohibition uses dürfen nicht. Darf nicht leer sein bans an empty value. muss nicht means need not and does not mean must not. Esperanto still needs explicit list and relative-time patterns because those two Intl formatters fall back to English. JSON-objekto is the shared repair term. enfermitaj en citiloj states quotation marks. A noun-derived verb remains possible and is not required here. resumo de memoroj is the memory-summary term. one is singular and other is plural.
